headline: Ad weakness drives sharp revenue and profit decline
summary_short: Net revenues fell 7.3% y/y to $410.2M and income from operations dropped 45.2% to $64.3M. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.06 versus $0.42 a year ago.
summary_long: Advertising revenue declined on weaker demand from e-commerce, online game and cosmetic advertisers, partly offset by internet service, handset and automobile sectors. Alibaba ad revenue fell 33% against a high base. Costs rose 6% on ad production costs, cutting operating margin to 16% from 27%. Cash and short-term investments were $2.31B. MAUs were 551M and DAUs 254M. No guidance was given.
confidence_notes: US-GAAP release (6-K EX-99.1). Shard EPS ($0.06) is the company's non-GAAP diluted figure; its y/y prior in the shard ($0.93) does not match the release's $0.42, so the q/q delta (vs $0.28) is shown for EPS. Prior-year GAAP net income included a one-off deferred tax and equity pick-up effect, which exaggerates the y/y decline.

drivers.explanation: Advertising fell on demand divergence across industries, with less revenue from e-commerce, online game and cosmetic sectors, partly offset by internet service, handset and automobile. VAS slipped on lower game-related revenue.
Alibaba ad revenue fell 33% due to a high comparison base from last year's local service promotion budget. Excluding Alibaba, advertising fell 5%.
Costs and expenses rose 6%, mainly from increased ad production costs, while revenue fell, so operating margin dropped to 16% from 27%.
